what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Move from a CRM spreadsheet to Drive folders first
sections.para: Someone running relationships in a spreadsheet cannot jump straight to encrypted vaults, but Google Workspace and a Claude seat get most of the way. Each row becomes a Drive folder of plain documents, and a Claude Project's instructions act as the behaviour policy: draft and never send, append and never rewrite, stay in the folder.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: One folder per person, a six-line policy, five exercises
sections.para: Each person gets a Drive folder with a record, ledger, messages, notes and an agent-written summary. A Claude Project connected to Drive and Gmail holds a six-line policy. Migration takes an afternoon, five exercises build the habit, early mistakes are fixed by policy lines, and the vault comes later.

sections.label: What a spreadsheet cannot hold, and a folder can
sections.line: In a folder, the record is everything that happened
sections.para: A spreadsheet's record is a typed summary row; a folder keeps every message word for word, an append-only timeline where corrections are new lines, call notes and a summary rebuilt from the files beneath it. That reversal gives the agent something to work with, and lets a second reader see everything first.

sections.label: The folder
sections.line: Five named documents per person mirror the agents' structure
sections.para: A Contacts folder in Drive holds one folder per person with a Record doc citing sources, an append-only Ledger sheet, a Messages doc of every exchange word for word, a Notes doc for calls and voice notes, and a Summary the agent writes and nobody edits. It is the vault structure minus hashes and graph.

sections.label: The agent, and its policy
sections.line: A Claude Project's six-line instructions are the behaviour policy
sections.para: Connect Drive and Gmail in the Claude app and create a Contacts Project whose instructions say: draft and never send, write only into the person's folder, never change the Record without showing me, append and never rewrite, cite every fact, ask before reaching outside, and report each task in one line. Most of this is told, not enforced.

sections.label: The migration
sections.line: Migration takes one afternoon, then nothing is retyped
sections.para: Export the sheet as CSV, have the agent propose a folder and Record per row, make the folders from a template, then fill each Record from a year of Gmail with sources and correct it once. Generate summaries and fix errors in source documents. Afterwards the agent logs each email and call.

sections.label: Five exercises, from simple to harder
sections.line: Five exercises build the habit, from asking to campaigns
sections.para: Over the first week: ask who has not been contacted in a month, prepare a meeting brief from the folder, draft a follow-up without sending, debrief a call by voice note into Notes and the Record, and run a campaign drafting personalised notes to everyone who cares about a topic. Each is one message.

sections.label: What it will get wrong, and the fix
sections.line: Two predictable mistakes, each fixed by a policy line
sections.para: The agent will put unsourced facts or inferred stages in the Record, fixed by a stricter line sending unsourced facts to Notes as inference. It will drop something from the Summary, fixed by adding it to the Record and regenerating. Asking unexpectedly is not a mistake; it is the policy working.

sections.label: When to move the folders into a vault
sections.line: Move to a vault for sharing, secrecy or portability
sections.para: Three signals: a second agent or person's agent must read specific folders, which a vault's per-folder read key handles better; the files must be unreadable by Google and Workspace admins; or the record must travel between tools. Because the folder shape already matches, the move is a copy and the policy stays the same.

sections.label: For the agent that sends this
sections.line: The agent can send this with four substitutions
sections.para: When someone asks how contacts are run, the RiskMandate agent should send this article with the person's own name in the examples, their Workspace and Claude plan in the setup, three real contacts for exercises two to four, and their own topic for exercise five. Nothing else changes, especially not the policy.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Connectors change, most rules are told, scale is limited
sections.para: What the Drive and Gmail connectors allow is as of October 2026 and varies by plan, though reading and drafting suffice. Most of the policy is told rather than enforced, so the one-line report and a seat per agent matter. One afternoon covers twenty to fifty contacts; hundreds means batches and the vault signals.
